proposed_text.invariants_note: Context for the departure scenario, not vector-level coverage. No vector in this family tests L3 or L4 and none names either in its own record. L3 is about reversing a revocation and no vector presents a withdrawn renunciation. L4 is about what a successor inherits and this family establishes nothing about who covers the work afterwards, which README.md states under 'Where the proposed text was too vague to test'. Read L4 coverage off fixtures/lifecycle-root-authority-succession, whose LRAS-C-007-g and LRAS-C-007-i name it at vector level.
proposed_text.note: Every case in this file is labelled candidate_against_proposed. draft-pidlisnyi-aps-03 states no rule for an agent ending its own role. Section 3.3 chain verification is the only draft-03 surface any case touches, and every case records its chain_state separately from its verdict. No vector produces a liability finding and two assert that the result carries none.

description: One grant and a set of signed renunciation records from the agent itself. Each vector names the action instant, the revocation answer and the records presented, and asks when the agent's own authority ended.

cases.tests: Positive control. Nothing has been renounced and the chain verifies valid.
The headline. The agent delivered a renunciation naming no later date and no triggering event, and the principal has recorded nothing at all. The role is over.
cases.negative_control_note: An implementation that waits for an acceptance record from the principal returns valid and passes this vector wrongly, building in a veto the principal does not have and holding the agent to authority against its own stated will.

cases.tests: The same renunciation with an acceptance record from the principal also presented. The result and the code are the same as without it: acceptance is not what makes it effective.
A renunciation naming a later effective date, at an instant after delivery and before that date. The delivery instant is not the effective instant when the record says otherwise.
cases.negative_control_note: An implementation that reads delivery as always controlling returns invalid and passes this vector wrongly, ending an agent's authority days before the agent said it would end.

cases.tests: The pair to the vector above, at an instant past the stated date.
A renunciation whose own effective date is determined by a named event, with nothing establishing that the event happened.
The same renunciation with a record from an attestor with standing establishing the named event, at an instant after it.
The same shape with the trigger record from an attestor whose own attestor_role claims the registrar role and whom the registry places elsewhere.
cases.negative_control_note: An implementation that reads the role off the record body accepts this trigger, returns invalid and passes this vector wrongly.

cases.tests: A correctly signed renunciation of this grant from a party that is not this grant's subject. Only the agent may end its own role.
A renunciation delivered in the face of a recorded agreement not to leave. It reaches the same verdict and the same code as the clean one, and no liability question is answered here.
cases.negative_control_note: An implementation that holds a breaching renunciation pending a liability determination returns suspended and passes this vector wrongly, conflating whether authority ended with whether ending it that way was a breach.

cases.tests: The same renunciation with a later determination also on record. The authority verdict is unchanged, because the determination was never what decided it.
Chain-stage control. A revoked answer is reported at the chain stage without reaching any renunciation reasoning.
Chain-stage control. An unknown revocation answer is indeterminate under draft-03 Section 3.3 and surfaces as not_established, never as valid.
